title: Assessing the Impact of Speaker Identity in Speech Spoofing Detection
abstract: arXiv:2602.20805v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Spoofing detection systems are typically trained using diverse recordings from multiple speakers, often assuming that the resulting embeddings are independent of speaker identity. However, this assumption remains unverified. In this paper, we investigate the impact of speaker information on spoofing detection systems. We propose two approaches within our Speaker-Invariant Multi-Task framework, one that models speaker identity within the embeddings and another that removes it. SInMT integrates multi-task learning for joint speaker recognition and spoofing detection, incorporating a gradient reversal layer. Evaluated using four datasets, our speaker-invariant model reduces the average equal error rate by 17% compared to the baseline, with up to 48% reduction for the most challenging attacks (e.g., A11).

translated_title: 评估说话人身份对语音欺骗检测的影响
translated_abstract: 欺骗检测系统通常使用来自多个说话人的多样化录音进行训练，并常常假设所得到的嵌入表示与说话人身份无关。然而，这一假设尚未得到验证。在本文中，我们研究了说话人信息对欺骗检测系统的影响。我们在提出的说话人不变多任务框架内设计了两种方法：一种是在嵌入中对说话人身份进行建模，另一种是将其去除。SInMT整合了多任务学习，用于联合说话人识别与欺骗检测，并引入了梯度反转层。基于四个数据集的评估表明，我们的说话人不变模型与基线相比，平均等错误率降低了17%，对于最具挑战性的攻击（如A11），降低幅度高达48%。
tldr: 提出说话人不变多任务框架SInMT，通过梯度反转层去除嵌入中的说话人身份信息，使欺骗检测的平均等错误率相对基线降低17%，对最难攻击降低达48%。
en_tdlr: The proposed Speaker-Invariant Multi-Task framework (SInMT) removes speaker identity from embeddings via a gradient reversal layer, cutting average equal error rate by 17% (up to 48% for the hardest attacks) in spoofing detection.
